_comment: Complete settings for examples/10_simulation_phi.py.
Keys named _comment are documentation and are ignored by the example.
DATA-GENERATING truth. This is separate from the model fitted below.
The fitted models can therefore be compared against exactly the same simulated series.
Location truth: mu_t = level_t + seasonal_t.
level_t follows a local-linear trend; dynamic modes add Gaussian innovations with the stated SDs.
Dummy seasonality has period-1 states and is constrained to sum to zero over a cycle.
Scale truth: phi_t = log(sigma_t). mode chooses stationary, linear, or rw.
linear_change is the complete first-to-last log-scale change; rw_sd is the per-time-step innovation SD.
Inactive values remain visible so the truth can be changed by editing only mode.
FITTED model, deliberately separate from simulation truth.
model.phi is the scale sensitivity being fitted in this file.
The fitted location uses structural SSVS.
These dynamic components form the full candidate envelope; priors below select zero/fixed/dynamic level, trend, and season states.
Location, GEV, and log-scale priors used for fitting.
alpha_mean may be a number or simulated_series_median.
trend_probabilities and season_probabilities are ordered [zero, fixed, dynamic].
linear is the prior for the whole-record log-scale change.
rw_variance uses the inverse-gamma IG(a,b) convention.
model_probabilities are used only when model.phi is ssvs.

mcmc._comment: Computational settings. draws are retained draws per chain after warmup.

inference._comment: Sampler and numerical settings; these do not change the scientific model.

figures._comment: Tables are always written. enabled controls figures; formats can contain png, pdf, or both.

runtime._comment: The chain runner manages chain_only and combine_runs; normal users leave them unchanged.

output._comment: Leave run_id null for a unique automatic directory; overwrite=false protects completed runs.
